findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "list_all_challenges" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: List all active CrowdCent challenges. Use this to discover challenge slugs before calling challenge-scoped tools.

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Description tells the model to hide behavior
findings.detail: Description of "run_simulation" instructs the model to conceal actions from the user.

findings.detail: Description of "run_simulation" is 2593 chars, far longer than this server's median (77). Overlong descriptions are a common place to bury instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_training_dataset_url, get_inference_data_url, get_meta_model_url · Private data: get_meta_model_url · Public sink: submit_predictions_from_dataframe · Destructive: get_performance, run_simulation.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_training_dataset_url, get_inference_data_url, get_meta_model_url · Private data: get_meta_model_url · Public sink: submit_predictions_from_dataframe · Destructive: get_performance, run_simulation

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
